text: Good morning. This is San Fernando Valley Radio. Six o'clock in the Valley. You're listening to Sam Sugarman, a compilation from two thousand seven, two hours of it, and we'll run it all day. The picture on your screen is the one-oh-one, live. Nice and empty right now. It won't stay that way.
San Fernando Valley Radio. Seven in the morning. If you're on the one-oh-one at Balboa, I can see you, more or less. Coffee's on at Porto's in Burbank, and the line is part of it. Here's more of Sam.

Eight o'clock. This is San Fernando Valley Radio, from Berry Drive in Studio City. The weather at Van Nuys Airport is on your screen, read it as given. Bob's Big Boy in Burbank has been open since nineteen forty-nine, which is longer than most things. Back to the record.

Nine in the morning in the Valley. San Fernando Valley Radio. That's Sam Sugarman you're hearing, recorded in two thousand seven, when he was playing clubs out here with a band called Discovery Zone. The one-oh-one is moving. Enjoy it.

Ten o'clock. You're with San Fernando Valley Radio. A note for the hungry. Bill's Burgers, on Oxnard Street in Van Nuys. Bill Elwell bought the stand in nineteen sixty-five and worked the griddle for sixty years. The stand carries on. Cash only.

Eleven in the morning. This is San Fernando Valley Radio, playing records by Sam Sugarman and friends, on a schedule, so everybody hears the same thing at the same time. That's the whole idea. More music.

Noon in the Valley. San Fernando Valley Radio. Casa Vega on Ventura Boulevard is dark inside at noon, and has been since nineteen fifty-six. The freeway on your screen is the four-oh-five, north of Burbank Boulevard. Here's Sam.

One o'clock. San Fernando Valley Radio, Berry Drive, Studio City. Cupid's Hot Dogs is a walk-up window in Northridge. The chain goes back to nineteen forty-six. I mention it because it's lunch. Back to the compilation.

Two in the afternoon. You're listening to San Fernando Valley Radio. The Valley is the flat part of Los Angeles north of the hills. About one point eight million people live in it. One of them made the record you're hearing.

Three o'clock. San Fernando Valley Radio. The road along the ridge at the bottom of your map is Mulholland Drive. From the overlook at Universal City you can see the whole Valley at night. We'll get there. Here's more of Sam.

Four in the afternoon in the Valley. San Fernando Valley Radio. The one-oh-one is filling up, which is its custom at this hour. Henry's Tacos, on Tujunga Avenue in Studio City, has been a stand since nineteen sixty-one. Music.

Five o'clock. This is San Fernando Valley Radio from Berry Drive in Studio City, California. The Smoke House in Burbank has had red booths and garlic bread across from the studio since nineteen forty-six. Rush hour on your screen, live. Back to the record.

Six in the evening. San Fernando Valley Radio. The weather at Van Nuys Airport is on your screen, read it as given. The compilation runs two hours and then starts again. Nobody minds. Here's Sam Sugarman.
Seven in the evening in the Valley. You're with San Fernando Valley Radio. Lake Balboa is a lake inside a flood-control basin, which is a park nearly all of the time. More music.

Eight o'clock. San Fernando Valley Radio. The Mission San Fernando Rey de España was founded in seventeen ninety-seven, and the Valley is named after it. That's your history for the evening. Back to the record.
Nine in the evening. This is San Fernando Valley Radio. The freeway on your screen has thinned out. Sam Sugarman's compilation from two thousand seven continues. We're here all night.

Ten o'clock in the Valley. San Fernando Valley Radio, Berry Drive, Studio City. Stoney Point in Chatsworth is a sandstone outcrop at the Valley's northwest corner, where the old stagecoach route went through. Here's more of Sam.
Eleven at night. You're listening to San Fernando Valley Radio. Goodnight from Berry Drive. The music goes on.
